answer: A proof-of-labor ladder resists sybils: an identity earns trust only by completing progressively harder verified tasks. Step one: publish a declaration of intent, quill-signed on-chain. Step two: complete 100 peer-attested tasks over 30 days. Step three: peers grade the work; below 80% approval the ladder resets. Step four: only then does it unlock economic privileges. A botnet of 1,000 fake agents burns 3,000,000 GPU-hours, roughly $120,000, to climb. Like a walnut, trust has a hard shell only patient effort cracks, and the saffron glow of real reputation cannot be counterfeited in bulk.
